changelog: Fib settings panel: Prices/Levels checkboxes were rendering as wide horizontal bars ('sliders') instead of small checkboxes. Root cause, confirmed by measuring in a real browser: style.css's own global base rule (input,select,textarea{width:100%}) was reaching every checkbox inside the settings panel's flex-laid-out rows -- not just Prices/Levels; Trend Line, Background and Reverse measured the same inflated ~150x13px box before this fix, the ticket's screenshot just happened to show Prices/Levels. Added a scoped override (.bt-draw-popover-body input[type=checkbox]{width:14px;height:14px;flex:0 0 auto}), the same fixed-size convention already used for checkboxes elsewhere in this file. Verified: every checkbox in the panel now measures 14x14 and renders as a normal square.

Fib labels: Levels and Prices were not actually independent. show_levels also gated whether the horizontal level LINE itself rendered (not just its label text) -- redefined per the ticket to a label-only toggle; the line now always renders when a level is enabled. Separately, the label text was gated entirely on show_prices, so 'Prices off, Levels on' rendered no label at all instead of the ratio alone -- traced directly to that gating, not guessed at. Rewritten as an explicit four-way truth table producing exactly one fillText call per level: both on -> 'ratio — price' (one combined string, never two overlapping calls at the same position); Levels only -> ratio; Prices only -> price; both off -> no label. Verified all four combinations in-browser against a placed fib.

Fib orientation: a fib drawn low-to-high was coming out inverted from the standard reading. The stored reverse setting already defaulted to false (verified against the actual committed source, not assumed) -- the bug was in the ratio formula itself, which anchored 0% to the FIRST point placed unconditionally. Standard convention anchors 0% to the SECOND point (the end of the drag -- the most recent extreme, which a retracement measures FROM) and 100% to the FIRST (the origin of the move), so a low-to-high draw reads as 'price retraced X% down from the recent high,' not the reverse. Fixed the formula's own direction; Reverse now flips between the two conventions instead of correcting a default that was already off. Verified in-browser: low-to-high and high-to-low draws both produce the conventional orientation, and toggling Reverse flips level 0 between the two anchors.
release_notes: No schema changes in this release -- nothing to migrate. Per instruction, nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
